then.prompt: Remove a +1{p} counter from this weapon?

_comment:
'Target weapon attack gets "When this hits a hero, you may remove a +1{p} counter from this weapon. If you do, destroy an aura they control."' Warrior Attack Reaction.

TARGET: ATTACK_REACTION is the proven shape for a hand-played attack reaction whose target.filter is checked at play legality (play.py _legality_check lines 420-431 evaluate cd.abilities target_filter against state.combat); ironsong_response_blue (hp, shipped) targets a weapon attack the same way. ATTACK_IS_WEAPON (condition_types.py:198) reads combat.from_weapon - exactly 'weapon attack'.

INJECTION: INJECT_TRIGGER scope COMBAT (default) with the NESTED trigger dict - required, because a top-level conditions key would be popped by the loader as an effect-level gate evaluated once at registration, when there may be no attack. ON_HIT dispatches to combat.attack_card, which for a weapon attack IS the weapon itself (dawnblade precedent), so 'this weapon' is the card every inner effect resolves against, whoever played Dice Up.

COUNTER KIND IS 'power' (lowercase): that is the kind _recalculate_attack_power feeds from (card.counters['power']); kinds are case-sensitive dict keys and '+1{p}' would match nothing.

GATE VIA CONDITIONAL, NOT MAY-LEVEL CONDITIONS: INJECT_TRIGGER compiles inner effects at fire time from the RAW dicts (effect_types.py:2148-2149), bypassing the loader's conditions-pop (loader.py:87), so a 'conditions' key on the inner MAY would be silently unread there. CONDITIONAL reads 'when' at runtime (:3708), so HAS_COUNTER gates whether the prompt is offered at all - 'you may remove...' implies a counter exists, and without the gate accepting the prompt with zero counters would still destroy an aura (remove_counter removes min(current, amount)).

REMOVE_COUNTERS AS EFFECT, NOT COST: the same-named COST reads player.counters keyed (slug, zone, counter) (cost_types.py:548-573), not card.counters where weapon counters live - it could never pay for this. The EFFECT defaults its target to [card] (:5042) and routes through the canonical remove_counter, so actual removal emits RemoveCounterEvent.

AURA DESTROY: DESTROY_PERMANENT subtype Aura player OPPONENT amount 1 is the shipped spelling (bet/smack_of_reality_red.json). OPPONENT resolves relative to the attack's controller, i.e. the hero hit ('they', guaranteed by ATTACK_TARGET_IS_HERO); with several auras the handler asks which to destroy, matching the release note 'You choose which aura they control to destroy'.

RELEASE NOTES need nothing extra authored: removing a counter mutates card.counters, so static continuous effects conditioned on the count re-evaluate at the next recalculation naturally, and layer-continuous timing is engine-side.
